subject.title: Model configuration accepts unvalidated model names, enabling silent misconfiguration

question: Should unknown configured model refs be warning-only in config validate/doctor, hard validation errors, or left to runtime/startup handling when catalog authority is incomplete?
rationale: The code can identify configured refs, but the permanent behavior affects custom providers, local proxies, future model names, fail-closed config validation, and upgrade safety.

options.title: Warning-first validation
options.body: Add catalog-backed config validate and doctor warnings for unknown configured refs, while keeping existing configs loadable by default and distinguishing custom or untrusted catalog cases.

options.title: Strict validation
options.body: Reject unknown configured refs at validation time, accepting a compatibility break unless maintainers also define an escape or migration contract.

options.title: Runtime-only handling
options.body: Keep config validation permissive and rely on startup checks, runtime errors, and fallback notices instead of adding a new config/doctor analyzer.

recommendation.title: Warning-first validation
recommendation.body: Add catalog-backed config validate and doctor warnings for unknown configured refs, while keeping existing configs loadable by default and distinguishing custom or untrusted catalog cases.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest current-source routing candidate for the validation and fallback-notice lines involved in the decision.
